newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: High money rates keep Sri Lanka rupee up.
newsitem.headline: High money rates keep Sri Lanka rupee up.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed higher as bankers sold dollars rather than pay high holding costs as money rates rose, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57 to the dollar after opening at 57.03, up from its previous closing level of 57.07. The dollar fell to a low of 56.96 but bounced back to 57.08 on import covering.
"Banks sold dollars due to the high cost of holding the currency, which resulted from volatile call money rates," said a Citibank dealer.
"Without underlying trade demand, the dollar would have fallen much further," he said.
Overnight call money traded between 20 and 29 percent due to a number of big borrowers coming into the market, and closed at 25 percent, dealers said.
Money has been tight since last week, when banks began buying dollars from the Central Bank and the government drew on treasury accounts in state banks.
"Call money will open high on Thursday too. Money valued for Thursday was done on Wednesday at 26 percent," said an American Express Bank dealer.
